_**Agent (copilot/claude-sonnet-4.6)**_

Да, через `Listenable.merge` — он объединяет несколько `Listenable` (которым является `ValueNotifier`) в один, срабатывающий при изменении любого из них:

```dart
ListenableBuilder(
  listenable: Listenable.merge([vm.isSearchVisible, vm.searchQuery]),
  builder: (context, _) {
    final isVisible = vm.isSearchVisible.value;
    final query = vm.searchQuery.value;
    // ...
  },
)
```

Это эквивалент `combineLatest2` — билдер перестраивается при изменении любого из notifier-ов, а значения читаются напрямую через `.value`.

When app goes to background: `isActive = false` → `Deny` emitted → `setDeniedAtIfNeeded()` → `_deniedAt` is set → `_performAuthorizationIfNeeded` returns `Deny` (which shows blur)


When app comes back to foreground: `isActive = true` → `Allow` emitted, but `_performAuthorizationIfNeeded` checks if the inactivity period has exceeded the max duration. So when the app goes to background again immediately after, the `Deny` event is emitted but `setDeniedAtIfNeeded()` doesn't update `_deniedAt` because it's already set, meaning the blur never appears.

After the first cycle completes with a `Deny` emission, the distinct operator has `Deny` as its last cached value. When the app comes back to foreground and emits `Allow`, the distinct operator sees a different type and passes it through. But then when the app quickly goes to background again, it tries to emit another `Deny`—except the distinct operator still has `Deny` cached from before, so it blocks the duplicate and never passes it downstream to the `asyncMap`. So the `Deny` event does reach `asyncMap` and should trigger the blur.
